issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Emit a events when resize status changes
issue_context.body:
/kind feature

To help with debugging in place pod resize, the Kubelet should emit events along with various resize status changes:

1. Resize accepted: report the resource deltas
2. Resize infeasible: which resources were over capacity
3. Resize deferred: which resources were over available capacity
5. Resize completed
6. Resize error

/sig node
/priority important-longterm
/milestone v1.32
/triage accepted

Yes, I think so, there are two reasons:
- If Resize status is set as ResizeDeferred (because there is no available resource),  ResizeDeferred event is print, but after node has available resource, Resize will be completed, but no message to indicate it.
- In pod description, limit and request cpu/memory are updated according to the patch command，this does not mean that resize has been successfully applied. Complete event will be helpful for user to make next its next operation.

@sftim Some questions raised on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130387 about the resize completed event that I'd be interested in your perspective on:
1. What should the contents of the event message be? The PR is proposing dumping the allocated CPU & memory resources for all containers, but I'm worried that message can get quite large. Maybe with better formatting it wouldn't be so bad though.
2. For a resize that doesn't change the actual resources at all, should the resize completed event be emitted? I think this will only happen if a Deferred or Infeasible resize is reverted

EDIT: After further discussion, I'm recommending we keep reporting the full pod allocation (in a more condensed format), and emit the event any time the resize status is cleared (including reverting deferred or infeasible resizes)

If it's feasible to include the extra information (eg current Pod limits and requests) in an annotation, maybe do that. Events can have annotations IIRC.
But I wouldn't block a merge on covering that part. I don't recommend putting that level of detail into `note`.

> For a resize that doesn't change the actual resources at all, should the resize completed event be emitted?

I don't have an opinion, but it would be nice if the event `reason` can make it clear whether a resize actually happened.
